title: Kernel-hint propagation + progressive prefill shaper to reduce tail latency
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: We still observe 99.9th percentile token latency spikes (~2-4x higher than p95) for mixed short/long workloads under sustained load. Investigation points to two interacting factors: (1) poor kernel fit when admission time decisions are made without recent kernel performance hints (especially for heterogeneous model variants and quantized kernels), and (2) coarse prefill shaping that inserts full-prefill work into batches that would have benefitted from progressive prefill / decode overlap.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight kernel-hint propagation layer in the admission path plus a progressive prefill shaper. The kernel-hint layer attaches a small prediction payload (kernel_affinity_hint, expected_seq_len_bucket, latency_percentile_hint) to queued requests; the batch shaper uses these hints to form batches that (a) maximize kernel homogeneity and (b) schedule partial prefill slices earlier for long-sequence requests so decode can overlap with remaining prefill work. This aims to reduce straggler-induced tail latency and improve throughput without sacrificing p95.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Where to compute hints: options are client-side (SDK) vs inference gateway vs admission proxy. We choose admission proxy to keep SDK footprint small and allow runtime telemetry feedback loops. 2) Hint accuracy vs payload size: use discrete buckets (short/medium/long sequence, int8/fp16/4-bit quant) to keep propagation payload <64 bytes. 3) Prefill slicing granularity: 8-token slices for long sequences performed opportunistically; too small slices increase kernel dispatch overhead, too large slices reduce overlap benefits — 8 is the experimental sweet spot. 4) Backwards compatibility: hints are optional; admission path must fall back to current heuristic when missing.

Implementation plan: 1) Add KernelHint struct to admission metadata and wire it through request context (admission proxy -> batcher -> kernel scheduler). 2) Update batch shaping algorithm to prefer grouping by kernel_affinity_hint and seq_len_bucket using a weighted scoring function that balances utilization and latency SLO. 3) Implement progressive prefill: long requests emit initial prefill slice that can be decoded in parallel with remainder prefill; decoder threads consume as soon as a coherent prefix of KV cache is available. 4) Metrics and gates: add per-hint histograms for token latency, batch composition distribution, kernel switch ratio, and decode overlap percentage.

Success criteria: 20-40% reduction in p99 token latency for mixed short/long traffic in canary traffic, no regression in p50/p95, <5% throughput regression for steady-state CPU/GPU utilization.

Rollout and rollback: Canaries on dev->staging (10% traffic) then production canary (5% of requests by region) for 48 hours, monitor token latency dashboards and kernel switch rate. Rollback if p99 increases by >10% relative to baseline or if kernel error ratio increases >0.1%.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Priya Menon: Initial spike analysis attached: links to internal dashboard and flame graphs (confluence: /d/srv/prefill-tail-analysis). Observed frequent kernel switching within single batches when mixed quantization requests co-locate.

2026-02-22 - Luca Moretti: Prototype kernel hint encoding in admission proxy completed. Encoding uses three bytes: quant_bucket, seq_bucket, recent_latency_bucket. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/tree/feat/kernel-hint-proxy PR: #4123.

2026-02-25 - Mei Chen (SRE): Observed small latency around admission loop after enabling hint propagation under synthetic load (+0.8ms median). This is acceptable but we should optimize serialization path.

2026-03-01 - Design review (with Alex R.): Confirmed progressive prefill UX for callers: no API change, hints are internal-only. Need to document caveats for streaming clients about slight reordering of prefix availability.
2026-03-04 - Experiment 1: Staging A/B with static hint grouping: p99 down by 18% for the 60/40 short/long mix. Kernel-governed batching reduced kernel switch ratio by 35%.

2026-03-08 - Engineering note (Luca): Tuned shaper scoring weights after observing over-aggressive isolation of long requests causing utilization drop. New weights maintain utilization within -2% of baseline while preserving tail reduction.

2026-03-12 - QA: Added tests for hint absence fallback, and for progressive prefill reassembly correctness. Test PR: #4298. QA observed a decoding edge-case when slice boundaries aligned with layer norm boundary; fixed by adjusting slice aligner.
notes: Next steps: finalize production perf tests (multi-region), add automated canary gating in the console, and prepare runbook for rollback. Schedule a 30-minute sync with SRE and Runtime on 2026-03-15.
